fields.description: AmbiSort A-Series is Ambi Robotics’ configurable small-parcel sorting system for sacks or totes. A soft-touch gripper transfers parcels across four barcode scanners and two quality-control zones to a gantry; operators seal and replace full sacks. The current configurator’s 66 destinations is explicitly a mock placeholder, while an older Q3 2022 deck describes 66 sacks for a particular historical customer layout and names an A-Series v2 schematic. A November 2024 manufacturer case report gives 355 sorts/h in 2022, 410 in 2023 and 500 after 2024 upgrades, with 99.6% sort accuracy in the latter context. These dated customer figures are not a guaranteed current rating or dimensional vision precision. Generic AmbiSort 2020 production does not establish this named generation’s first release.

fields.description: AmbiStack is Ambi Robotics’ configurable overhead stacking system, publicly introduced January 28, 2025. The current FAQ permits cases up to 50 lb each and 52×32×32 in; those are handled-case limits, not robot mass, dimensions or aggregate multi-pick capacity. A June 30, 2026 company release reports integration with Pickle Robot’s separate truck-unloading machines; 2025 deployment targets and current complete-system price/stock remain distinct.

highlights: Gantry robot system stacks mixed cases onto pallets or into containers
Vision, barcode tracking and online stack planning support inbound and outbound handling
Output positions and internal conveyors are configurable; operators replenish completed positions

The current FAQ specifies cases up to 50 lb each and 52 in long×32 in wide×32 in tall. These are handled-item limits, not machine mass, machine outer dimensions, total pallet load or a rated aggregate two-case gripper payload. Scan-tunnel configuration and palletizing rate depend on case size.

Sim2Real-based stack planning supports mixed cases without prior item-specific programming, and configurable SKU-based patterns are described. Dynamic multipicking can pick and place two cases together; the relative doubling claim is not an absolute cases-per-hour rating or universally achieved minimum.

Six, twelve or more output positions and pallet, cage, walled-container, floor and AMR-facing output choices are configurable layouts. The configurator also shows twelve locations using two machines. None of those choices establishes a separate robot model, fixed footprint, universal stacking-height limit or included AMR.

Light-curtain-guarded zones allow operators to remove/replenish pallets in one half while stacking continues in the other. The FAQ permits integration with external AMRs/AGVs. Operator work, replenishment and application-specific guarding remain part of the system; 24/7 service support is not battery life or measured uninterrupted runtime.

The January 28, 2025 primary manufacturer release explicitly introduces AmbiStack, forecasting initial deployments from mid-year through fall and expanded manufacturing capacity by early 2026. Those were dated plans, not current stock proof. The June 30, 2026 manufacturer account separately reports a commercial Pickle Robot/AmbiStack integration.

In that June 2026 integration, Pickle Robot’s separate machines unload trailers and a conveyor feeds AmbiStack for identification, scanning and palletizing. The partner’s truck-unloading capability is not inherited as an onboard AmbiStack feature or counted as another Ambi-manufactured model; software/vision/service offerings retain separate roles.

highlights: The June 6, 2023 primary manufacturer release introduces B-Series with induction-only, end-to-end sortation and vision-based sorter-expansion configurations. The number of robotic cells and destinations is adjustable; conveyor/vision-only options are not additional independently identified robot models.

The launch states throughput exceeding 1,200 parcels/h. The linked 2023 guide’s footnote explicitly says its data is based on three induction cells; the current configurator separately says each pick cell adds 500 sorts/h. Those configuration and date contexts remain separate rather than turning 1,200/h into a single-arm guarantee or deriving an exact linear whole-system rate.

An intelligent multi-suction gripper singulates parcels from deep bins or conveyors, followed by a buffer/central conveyor and a six-sided scan tunnel. Barcode data or optional WMS integration determines routing; overhead vision monitors container fill and lights notify operators to replenish completed positions.

The 2023 launch claims accuracy above 99.5%, while the guide separately distinguishes sortable in-size parcels, correct outputs and desired uptime. These are different supplier metrics with unresolved test conditions, not numeric dimensional vision precision, universally certified performance or robot battery/runtime specifications.

A/B series remain separate named systems: A-Series uses four barcode scanners and two QC zones in its described sack workflow; B-Series uses six-sided scan-tunnel induction and configurable gaylord/other outputs. AmbiOS/AmbiAccess and 24/7 support are software/service roles; no current numeric complete-system purchase or RaaS price is established.

highlights: The July 27, 2021 primary manufacturer release explicitly introduces AmbiKit and describes an already-deployed five-robot picking line for subscription-box kitting. Five robots in that system is not five total kinematic axes or five independently named AmbiKit model identities; July 28 media coverage is a later report.

The current product page states 12 kits/minute, while the 2021 introduction reports up to 60 individual items/minute in commercial production. These units and contexts are not interchangeable, and no fixed five-item kit length is inferred by dividing the numbers.

The page allows operators to select up to 15 SKUs and place items in robot-directed areas. Operators pack completed kits and respond to replenishment requests. SKU choices are not 15 robot models or proof that every kit contains 15 items.

The product page claims 99% complete-kit rate; the 2021 release separately claims more than 99% order accuracy. These are supplier quality measures with unspecified test conditions, not a universal success guarantee or dimensional vision precision. Zero-training/changeover and 24-hour language do not establish robot battery duration or uninterrupted runtime.

AmbiOS, Sim2Real learning, quality-control notifications and operator interfaces support the kitting workflow. Software/skill licenses and the current AmbiVision trial belong to separate offerings; no complete-system numeric price, hardware mass/dimensions, exact gripper rating or current stock is established.

Selected primary pages identify AmbiSort A-Series, AmbiSort B-Series, AmbiStack and AmbiKit. B-Series was introduced June 6, 2023, AmbiStack January 28, 2025 and AmbiKit July 27, 2021. Generic AmbiSort production in 2020 and a Q3 2022 A-Series/v2 deck do not unambiguously establish the named A-Series first release.

A-Series current 66-destination illustration is a mock placeholder; the old deck’s 66-sack Pitney Bowes layout is a dated installation example. A November 2024 primary case report gives 355/410/500 sorts per hour for 2022/2023/2024 performance contexts, not a universal guaranteed present capacity.

B-Series launch claims over 1200 parcels/h; its guide describes a three-induction-cell configuration, while the current configurator says each pick cell adds 500 sorts/h. Configurable arm count, outputs and conveyor/vision-only options remain system configurations rather than extra named robots or evidence of universal linear scaling.

AmbiStack FAQ limits handled cases to 50 lb and 52×32×32 in; these are not complete-machine dimensions/mass or a rated aggregate multi-pick payload. Six/twelve/more pallet positions, two-machine layouts and varied container types stay configurable. The June 2026 integration uses Pickle Robot’s separate unloading machines upstream of AmbiStack.

AmbiKit’s 12 kits/minute is distinct from the 2021 release’s up-to 60 individual items/minute. Five-robot picking lines and selection of up to 15 SKUs do not establish five system DOF, fixed kit length or 15 model identities. Operators still replenish product and pack completed kits.

AmbiOS, PRIME-1, Sim2Real, AI Skill Suite apps and AmbiAccess provide software/AI/analytics/support roles. AmbiVision is an OCR/barcode/dimensioning scan tunnel with local processing and WMS integration, not an extra articulated robot; future weighing/damage/labeling/case-opening functions and free 30-day trial are not established present robot specifications or purchase prices.

Supplier order/kit/sortability/uptime and ANSI claims,10,000x training,relative throughput improvements and fleet volumes remain dated and attributed. Current complete-system prices/stock, independent whole-cell certification, exclusive USPs, full historical portfolio and market/search leadership remain unproven. Human work,light-curtain guarding and external AMRs remain explicit.
